title: Writing a paragraph in Spanish
subtitle: How to write an opinion or argument paragraph at B1–B2 — what the grader looks for and how to deliver it.

text.text: Every attempt is scored on four criteria, and each one counts. A paragraph with perfect grammar that ignores half the prompt scores low; so does a well-organised answer full of agreement errors. Aim for a balance.
— did you answer the prompt, cover every required element, take a clear position where one is asked for, and stay inside the word range?
— does the paragraph have a clear opening, supporting points and a conclusion, and do connectors show how each idea relates to the last?
— is your word choice precise and varied, and does it fit the register (informal or formal) of the task?
— are verb forms, agreement and word order correct, and do you use some more complex structures (subordinate clauses, a range of tenses) accurately?
80–120 words, 15 minutes on the timer.
150–200 words, 25 minutes on the timer.
Going far over the maximum does not earn extra credit — it usually means repetition, which costs you on Coherence.
A strong opinion paragraph has three parts: an
that states your position,
(each backed by a reason or an example, and ideally one point that admits the other side), and a
that restates your view.
Here is a model paragraph answering

(is remote work a good thing?), one sentence at a time. It is 128 words — a little over the B1 maximum (120) and short of the B2 minimum (150). At B1, drop the example sentence (to about 104 words); at B2, add a reason or example to each point.

target.text: En mi opinión, el teletrabajo tiene más ventajas que inconvenientes.

body.en: In my opinion, remote work has more advantages than disadvantages.

note.text: Opening sentence: states the position clearly.

target.text: , permite ahorrar mucho tiempo,
no hay que desplazarse a la oficina todos los días.

body.en: Firstly, it saves a lot of time, since you don't have to travel to the office every day.

target.text: , una amiga mía tardaba casi dos horas en llegar al trabajo y ahora dedica ese tiempo a hacer deporte.

body.en: For example, a friend of mine used to take almost two hours to get to work, and now she spends that time doing sport.

target.text: , muchas personas se concentran mejor en casa, lejos del ruido y de las interrupciones constantes.

body.en: Moreover, many people concentrate better at home, away from noise and constant interruptions.

target.text: , no todo es positivo: trabajar en solitario puede provocar aislamiento, y es importante que las empresas organicen reuniones presenciales de vez en cuando.

body.en: However, not everything is positive: working alone can lead to isolation, and it is important that companies organise in-person meetings from time to time.

note.text: Supporting point 3 admits the other side. Note the subjunctive

target.text: el contacto con los compañeros es necesario, no hace falta ir a la oficina cada día para mantenerlo.

body.en: Although contact with colleagues is necessary, you don't need to go to the office every day to keep it up.

note.text: ), because the speaker accepts it as a fact.

target.text: , creo que un modelo mixto, con dos o tres días en casa, es la mejor solución.

body.en: In conclusion, I think a hybrid model, with two or three days at home, is the best solution.

note.text: Closing sentence: restates the position in a more precise form.

text.text: The connectors (highlighted) carry the argument: they tell the reader which sentence is a new point, which is an example, and where the paragraph turns to the other side.
At B1–B2 the grader looks for
: not just
and
, but connectors that show contrast, consequence and concession.

target.text: El transporte público es barato;
, contamina menos que el coche.

items.en: Public transport is cheap; moreover, it pollutes less than the car.

target.text: Las redes sociales nos conectan;
, también pueden aislarnos.

items.en: Social media connects us; however, it can also isolate us.

target.text: Los alquileres han subido mucho;
, muchos jóvenes viven con sus padres.

items.en: Rents have risen a lot; therefore, many young people live with their parents.

target.text: Algunas ciudades,
Barcelona, han limitado los pisos turísticos.

items.en: Some cities, such as Barcelona, have restricted tourist flats.

target.text: , el problema tiene solución si todos colaboramos.

items.en: In conclusion, the problem can be solved if we all work together.

text.text: With the
it concedes a fact you accept; with the
it concedes something hypothetical or not yet known.
At B2 you will also meet the subjunctive with a known fact the speaker treats as irrelevant:

children.text: Aunque sea tu jefe, no tiene razón

target.text: Aunque llueve, salgo a correr.

children.en: Although it is raining, I'm going for a run.

note.text: Indicative: it is raining right now.

target.text: Aunque llueva mañana, saldré a correr.

children.en: Even if it rains tomorrow, I'll go for a run.

note.text: Subjunctive: maybe it will rain, maybe not.

An informal message to a friend:

target.text: Querida Ana: ¿Qué tal? Hace mucho que no te escribo.

body.en: Dear Ana, how are you? I haven't written to you in a long time.

note.text: Informal opening; colon after the greeting.

target.text: Un abrazo,

body.en: Best wishes / Love,

text.text: A formal email or letter:

target.text: Estimado señor López:

body.en: Dear Mr López,

note.text: Formal opening. To an unknown reader:

target.text: Le escribo para solicitar información sobre el curso de verano.

body.en: I am writing to request information about the summer course.

target.text: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.

body.en: I look forward to your reply.

target.text: Atentamente,

body.en: Yours sincerely,

sections.title: the task and the word count

text.text: Most prompts list
— things your text must mention. The grader checks each one. Make every element visibly present: give it its own sentence, and use the element's own key word so it cannot be missed.

target.text: Una desventaja del teletrabajo es el aislamiento.

body.en: One disadvantage of remote work is isolation.

note.text: Required element "mention a disadvantage" — the key word

text.text: Before you write, list the required elements and give each one a sentence. Add your opening and closing sentence to the plan.
Draft the sentences, then join them with connectors so the reasoning is easy to follow.
before you submit, and compare with the range for your level.
Add a reason or a concrete example to your weakest point, or a sentence that admits the other side.
Cut repetition first — sentences that say the same thing twice — not a required element.
